notes.provenance: HAND-AUTHORED, and deliberately by a producer that does not exist: `recorder: {name: "future-recorder", version: "3.1.0"}` on a host called "some-other-runtime". Every unknown thing in it is a plausible v2.1 addition rather than a random key, because the question the fixture asks is what a CURRENT reader does with a FUTURE file, and a reader that copes with garbage may still drop a field it half-recognises.
notes.what_this_fixture_is_for: Spec §11's preservation rule — "unknown fields and unknown event types MUST survive load → save SEMANTICALLY INTACT: every key and value preserved; formatting, key order and numeric spelling are free" — plus §5.8's skip-unknown-events rule. The conformance runner's `semantic preservation` test loads this file through the tolerant profile and compares every top-level key against the parsed original, so a loader that whitelisted keys, or that defaulted anything INSIDE a segment, turns it red.
notes.unknown_at_every_level: Seven levels carry something the spec does not define, so a loader cannot pass by preserving only the easy ones: TOP (`recorder_build`, `eye_tracking`); inside a declared OBJECT (`viewport.orientation`); inside a session ARRAY element (`stylesheets[0].origin`); SEGMENT (`difficulty`); inside `initial_state` (`pointer_lock`); inside a DomNode (`intrinsic_size` on the img); on a known EVENT (`dom.text.reason`, `mouse.click.pressure`); and as whole unknown EVENT TYPES (`gaze.fixation`, `vendor.marker`). The last of these also carries an event-level `extensions` block, which §9 puts at session, segment AND event level and which nothing else in the corpus exercises at event level.
notes.why_strict_valid_is_false_and_that_is_CO: §5.8 has two halves and they point opposite ways: players MUST skip event types they do not recognise, and producers MAY NOT emit vendor events as top-level unknown types (they belong in `extensions`). So this file is exactly what a conforming PLAYER must load and exactly what a conforming PRODUCER must not write, and the two profiles say so separately — strict names the two unknown types, tolerant loads the file clean with no warnings. A fixture that was strict-valid could not make that point. This is the corpus's only entry where `expect: accept` and `strict_valid: false` coexist without a defect being alleged.
notes.unknown_FIELDS_are_not_errors: Note what is NOT in strict_errors: none of the eleven unknown FIELDS. The validator type-checks declared fields and does not enumerate permitted keys, which is what makes §11's preservation rule implementable at all — a strict profile that rejected unknown keys would forbid the forward compatibility the same document requires.
notes.the_tie_is_a_positive_claim: Events 3, 4 and 5 all sit at t=900, and the three spot checks pin that. §7: "within one array, array order is authoritative" at equal `t`, so a tie is CONFORMANT and a player must replay dom.attr(class) → dom.attr(alt) → scroll.window in that order. `negative-unsorted-events.json` is the refusal case (a DECREASE), and without this tie an implementation could satisfy that fixture by rejecting ties too, with nothing to notice.
notes.reference_checking_stops_at_unknown_type: `gaze.fixation` carries `node: 2`, which happens to resolve — but the corpus reference check does not look at it, because NODE_REF_FIELDS is keyed by event type and an unknown type has no declared reference fields. Guessing that any field called `node` is a node id is exactly the heuristic that would misread `touches[].id`. So this fixture also pins the limit of that check.
notes.perf_frame: "absolute": origin 4000, ended_at_perf 6000, last observed moment 2000 on the wire clock. Non-zero and self-consistent, so this hand-authored entry pins the same reading the generated CH captures do — without depending on a re-cut to keep pinning it.
